In Connect Four, controlling the center and its adjacent columns is a primary strategy. The center column (index 3) is the most valuable because it is part of the greatest number of potential winning lines (horizontal, vertical, and both diagonals). Since player 'o' has already blocked player 'x' from building a vertical line in column 3, the optimal move for 'x' is to develop horizontal and diagonal potential in the neighboring columns.

Computerized solvers for Connect Four indicate that after the first two moves are made in the center column (d1, d2 in algebraic notation), the best moves for the first player ('x') are in the adjacent columns (c1 or e1), which correspond to column indices 2 and 4. These moves are typically evaluated as stronger than continuing in the center column (d3, or index 3).

Choosing column index 2 will allow player 'x' to begin forming horizontal and diagonal connections, maintaining the early-game initiative.
